summary: Strong bash scripts with proper error handling and lock management. All 5 tests verify add+skip paths. GitHub Actions workflow passes actionlint. Docker setup minimal with pinned base. Critical issue: safe-mode-rollback.yml uses undeclared community.general.telegram module; fails ansible-lint.

checks.set_euo_pipefail: OK — both last-known-good.sh and run.sh use set -euo pipefail
checks.trap_cleanup: OK — last-known-good.sh acquires lock with proper EXIT trap release_lock
checks.lock_management: PASS — acquire_lock() blocks on existing /var/lock/fabric-lkg.lock with 30sec timeout; idempotent tag checks prevent redundant updates

checks.concurrency_control: OK — group and cancel-in-progress prevent duplicate runs
checks.artifact_handling: OK — logs uploaded on failure with 7-day retention
checks.health_checks: OK — workspace-manager health endpoint tested before tasks

ansible.critical_issue: community.general.telegram module referenced but not declared/installed; ansible-lint fails with syntax-check[unknown-module]

checks.minimal_layers: OK — single RUN for apt-get updates+installs+cleanup reduces image size

checks.service_dispatch: OK — case statement covers workspace-manager, mnemonic-mcp, fabric-watchdog

issues.description: community.general.telegram module used without being installed or declared in requirements
issues.impact: Playbook fails ansible-lint and cannot run on target hosts without community.general collection installed
issues.fix: Option A: Install community.general collection in deployment. Option B (RECOMMENDED): Replace all community.general.telegram calls with curl approach (already used in line 184-189). curl avoids external dependencies and is more reliable in CI environments.

notes: T19 demonstrates solid engineering: bash scripts resilient with locks, tests comprehensive, Docker minimal and pinned, GitHub Actions clean. Single critical blocker: Ansible linting fails due to undefined telegram module. Recommend adopting curl for all notifications to eliminate external collection dependency.
